claim_scope: Four-turn clean rectangular two-sheet synthetic maternal-health workbook journey. This does not establish support for merged headings, stacked subtables, or cross-sheet analytical joins. The split candidate is compared with the preserved counted Antigravity CLI run.

noncritical_shortfalls: The page shows Nalanda 75% and Gaya 68% for 2023 but does not state their 7 pp gap as a separate insight.

faults: The final page remained on institutional delivery instead of the requested postnatal Gaya/Nalanda state, though controls could reach it.
A disabled-looking 2021 control remained after the request for only 2022 and 2023.
It invented High/Moderate performance labels absent from the workbook.
The narrow document overflowed by 304 px.
The elapsed time included a recorded 97-second preview-process intervention.
strengths: All inspected values, both requested changes and the seven-point 2023 gap were correct.
The page and exports clearly preserved formulas and both source sheets.
Its visual treatment was more varied and elaborate than the fixed split renderer.

pairwise.interpretation: On this clean workbook journey, the split path is stronger overall because it preserves the requested durable state, remains offline and finishes faster. Antigravity is stronger on the explicit seven-point gap and visual richness. This is not evidence for arbitrary workbook layouts or editor-product equivalence.

decision: Advance to PDF and structure-preserving workbook extraction. Do not generalise this clean two-sheet result; add merged-heading, stacked-subtable, cross-tab and plain-language recovery cases against Antigravity.
